name: Lisbon
tagline: Seven hills, trams and tiled streets
summary: Split Lisbon by hill: Alfama and the castle one day, Belém's monuments another, with a day trip to Sintra's palaces. Wear grippy shoes; the pavements are steep and slick.
seasonNote: July and August are hot and crowded; winter is mild but wet.
arrival: The metro's red line links the airport to the centre in about 30 minutes; taxis and ride-hailing are inexpensive.
gettingAround: Walk within each district and use the metro, trams and funiculars between hills. Tram 28 has long queues; ride it early or use it one way.
cashTip: Cards work almost everywhere; keep coins for small bakeries and kiosks.
foodTip: Try pastéis de nata warm, grilled sardines in season, bacalhau and a bifana sandwich.
buyTip: Tinned fish, cork goods and hand-painted tiles from shops that name the maker; never buy antique tiles from street sellers.

connections.note: Alfa Pendular and Intercidades trains from Santa Apolónia or Oriente; book ahead for the best fares.
Air time only; add airport transfers.
Limited direct flights; buses take about 6 to 7 hours.

items.name: Belém Tower
items.summary: A 16th-century river fortress that became the symbol of Portugal's age of exploration.
items.expect: Queues to go inside and narrow one-way stairs; the outside is the main event.
items.tip: See it from the riverside first and go in only if the queue is short.

items.tip: Take an early train from Rossio and book Pena's timed ticket in advance.
